dbe_source.recommendation: Candidates did not square the RHS correctly. Write the RHS as (expression)^2 on its own line before expanding.

lesson.concept: Squaring the RHS means squaring the whole expression, not each term. (x - 2)^2 is not x^2 - 4. Write the bracket and expand properly.
lesson.why: The examiner wants to see the bracket written on its own line before expansion. That line earns a method mark.

example.problem: Square the right side of sqrt(2x + 5) = x - 3
work: Write the RHS as a bracket first: (x - 3)^2
Do not write x^2 - 9. That drops the middle term.

probe.problem: Square the right side of sqrt(3x - 1) = x + 2. Write the squared form before expanding.
probe.hint: Wrap the whole RHS in a bracket first.

learner_message: Squaring the right-hand side means squaring the whole expression. Write the bracket first, then expand.
